The capstone section "DINA scenarios against the ITER supply limits" lists, coil by coil, where DINA's demand passes a rating, with a table of every excursion. It does not show how a coil circuit is driven through a scenario, or which electrical risks that exposes. The lead asked on 19 October 2026 for a few clear figures instead: the integrated converter, coil and vessel model responding to one scenario playback, seen at the timescales where each risk lives, for normal operation, plasma initiation and fast discharge, and then again with the proposed filters inserted.

§1 — What each figure must show

Each risk shows on its own timescale, so each figure has three columns:

ColumnWindowCircuitRisk it exposes
pulse or eventthe whole 105069/3 playback, or the seconds around an SNU or FDU eventaveragedwhether the supply delivers DINA's current within its converter voltage and current ratings: saturation, circulating-current operation, and the discharge decay
rippleabout 40 ms, two mains cyclesswitchedthe 12-pulse ripple and the VS1 carrier at the coil and to ground, which the candidate output filters target
edgeabout 200 µs around one eventswitched, step-convergedthe fronts of commutation notches, IGBT edges, SNU insertion and FDU opening, which set the terminal-to-ground, worst-section and first-turn peaks

The rows are quantities, each against its own limit: coil current with the supply rating and the bridge mode (pulse column only, because it does not move on the fast scales); converter and coil voltage with the converter rating; both coil terminals and the worst winding section to ground, against the 22HLVN v1.0 Table 4 steady column in normal operation and its fast-discharge column for the discharge case; and the across-coil and first-turn voltages in the edge column. The averaged trace is drawn over the switched one, red marks only a crossed limit, and a focus line marks where each zoom is taken.

The figures are one per concern, not one composite, because the events need their own windows and limit columns and three circuits at three timescales would not read as one figure. The layout below is a mockup from held arrays (PF1, 105069/3), not a result. It shows two things the build must change: coil current is flat on the fast scales, so it belongs to the pulse column alone, and the held edge window is not converged. The worst winding section reaches 1.51 kV to ground with a 2.5 µs step and 0.28 kV with a 10 µs step, a factor of five.

§2 — One figure grammar and one record for every case

Write scripts/figures/coil_circuit_playback.py, which draws any case from one playback record, and the record's schema beside it. A record holds the case and circuit names, the pulse and run, the averaged pulse arrays (time, coil current, converter voltage, coil voltage, high and low terminal to ground), the switched ripple window, the switched edge window (adding the worst winding section and the first turn), each limit with its value and source, and a step-convergence receipt for the edge window: its terminal and worst-section peaks at step h and h/2. The drawing follows §1 and the repository's figure rules, saves through figure_layout.save_figure, and draws a filtered case with the unfiltered response beneath it in the context grey and the filtered response in the filtered hue, as the converter-filter figures already do.

Done when a synthetic record renders all three columns and passes the save check, and tests/test_coil_circuit_playback.py shows the drawer refuses a record with a limit missing its source and a record whose edge peaks differ by more than 1 % between h and h/2, the step-convergence gate that shared-coil-supply-model §3 set and iter-switched-terminal-transients §11 applies to every window. The held 2.5 µs and 10 µs PF1 windows are the negative control for the second refusal. Write paths: the script, the test, and docs/figures/coil-circuit-playback.

§3 — Normal operation: PF2 and PF1 through 105069/3

Two records from the integrated simulation along 105069/3 that iter-switched-terminal-transients §6 builds on the shared model. PF2 is the circuit whose first winding mode, 595 Hz, sits nearest the 600 Hz 12-pulse line (winding resonance plan), and it carries the VS1 string through the shared PF2–PF5 nodes. Its ripple window is where the 600 Hz line at the coil terminals is largest, and its edge window the largest VS1 IGBT edge inside that ripple window. PF1 is thyristor only. Its ripple window is where the converter holds its 2.1 kV rating (near 303 s in this pulse), and its edge window the largest commutation-notch front there. Each window is chosen by that stated rule, not by eye, and the rule is written into the record.

Done when both records pass §2's convergence check, both figures render, and each record names its windows' times and the peak of every row against its limit. Data go to /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/power_convertor/data/iter/coil_circuit_playback.

§4 — SNU switching at plasma initiation: CS1

CS1 from the start of 105069/3: the event column spans 0–20 s, covering the switching-network insertion at initiation, its bypass at 3 s, and CS1's late branch from 3 s to 13 s (ConverterNetwork.add_switching_network; 778SPD v1.0 PDF 51–52, 83–85). The ripple window covers the insertion, and the edge window its front at the design rise times the initiation record bounds. Limits: CS1's converter rating, the 22HLVN steady column for CS1, and the across-coil envelope that record uses.

Done when the record passes §2's convergence check and its figure renders, with the insertion step and the front's peaks to ground, across the coil and on the first turn stated against those limits.

§5 — Fast discharge: CS1 from its largest current in 105069/3

A fast discharge of CS1 tripped at its largest current in the pulse, through the switched breaker-opening and discharge-unit insertion builder that iter-switched-terminal-transients §11 lands: the FDU breaker opens and the converter's make switch closes across the converter (778SPD v1.0 PDF 8, 37, 93). §11 itself builds the PF1, PF6, CS3L and one VS1-coupled coil insertions, not CS1, so this section applies that builder to CS1 and owns the CS1 record. The event column spans the current's decay in seconds, the ripple window the breaker opening, and the edge window the front into the discharge resistor, with the internal section voltages. The ground limit is the 22HLVN fast-discharge column (5.0 kV for every CS module).

Done when the record passes §2's convergence check and its figure renders, with the discharge peak to ground stated against 5.0 kV and the worst internal section named.

§6 — The proposed filters on PF2

The §3 PF2 case again, at the same windows, with the two candidate output filters the capstone's converter-filter section screens: the PF2 damped LC (0.5 mH added to the present 0.3 mH, a 1.4 mF shunt and a 2.8 mF, 0.6 Ω damper) and the VS1 damped RC (the existing 6.25 µH pole reactors, 2.2 µF and a 4.4 µF, 1.5 Ω damper), PF2_FILTER and VS_FILTER in scripts/iter/converter_filter_study.py. They are screening candidates, not selected ITER hardware, and that screen favours keeping the existing thyristor hardware, so the figure shows what the candidates would change, not a design decision. The unfiltered response from §3 is drawn beneath in grey. No filter is screened for CS1 or PF1, so they are not repeated.

Done when the record passes §2's convergence check and its figure renders, and the record states, with and without the filters, the 600 Hz line at the coil terminals and the edge column's peaks to ground and on the first turn.

§7 — The capstone section rebuilt on the figures

Rebuild the "DINA scenarios against the ITER supply limits" section of docs/research/coil-supply-model-arc.html, which scripts/figures/arc_overview.py --assemble joins from the partial docs/figures/coil-supply-arc/dina/section.html that scripts/figures/arc_dina.py writes. The section keeps its key-shortfall paragraph and margin figure and gains the figures of §3–§5, each with one paragraph naming the risk it exposes and the margin to its limit. The §6 figure goes in the converter-filter section, docs/figures/coil-supply-arc/filter/section.html from scripts/figures/arc_filter.py. The excursion table in docs/figures/coil-supply-arc/dina/excursions.html moves into the scenario screen record that scripts/iter/scenario_screen.py writes, and the retired per-coil waveform figures leave docs/figures/coil-supply-arc/dina. Done when the assembled capstone carries the new section, every cited figure resolves, and the excursion table is in the screen record.

§8 — The fast-discharge commutation circuit from IDM, and the FDU fronts rerun

§5 put CS1's fast-discharge peak to ground at 4.23–4.93 kV against the 5.0 kV fast-discharge reference, 1.4 % inside it at the high installed-loss bound. But the switched builder imposes the FDU voltage as a ramp over an assumed 10 µs rise, and the real unit is not that. Every TF, PF and CS fast-discharge unit carries a snubber across its commutation path: 4 mF, 0.1 Ω and about 1 µH in the IDM transient model. The PF/CS specification rates it 4,000 µF, 0.1 Ω, +10/−2 kV and 200 kJ, as two RC branches, without saying whether 4,000 µF is per branch or for the pair. The discharge resistor carries its own stray inductance, 94.9 → 20.6 µH on CS1 and 44.8 → 11.2 µH on PF2. A counterpulse circuit, 1.6 mF and 16 µH charged to 7.6–9.2 kV, forces the vacuum breaker's current zero, and the cables add a few µH each. All of these values, with their sources, are in the IDM register §5. At 44 kA, a 4 mF snubber holds the rise to about 11 V/µs, with a time constant near 0.5 ms through the resistor, against the 10 µs ramp assumed so far. So the §5 front, and the rise-time question it raised, have to be redone on the real circuit.

This section builds the FDU commutation circuit in the switched insertion builder in place of the imposed ramp: bypass opening, vacuum-breaker current zero by the counterpulse, and current transfer into the discharge resistor, with its stray inductance, and the snubber in parallel. Parameters come from the register, carried as cited constants. The resistor inductance is run at both ends of its range, and the snubber capacitance at 4 mF and at 8 mF, the two readings of the specification. It closes one guard defect from §4's review: the insertion negative control ran two mutations together, so log the first-turn pin's mutation alone.

Done when, for every PF and CS circuit, the circuit run with a lumped coil inductance, as the IDM transient model does, reproduces that model's peak coil-terminal voltage Udr (7JQSNL v1.3 Table 5: CS1 7.6 kV, PF2 4.4 kV, and so on), or the record states the difference and its cause. With the coil plant in place, the CS1 and PF2 FDU rows then give, at both loss bounds and both readings of the snubber, the peak terminal and worst-section voltage to ground against the 22HLVN fast-discharge column, the voltage across the resistor against S9BRS4's 10 kV limit, the across-coil peak, and the first turn against the 2.5 kV turn-to-turn reference. Each edge window passes the 1 % step check, or is drafted and says so. A crossing is a finding to report against the rating, never a defect to fit away. Negative control: with the snubber removed, the front steepens, and the record shows by how much. The first-turn pin fails under its own mutation alone. A separate FDU front figure, one per phenomenon by the figure-count decision, draws CS1's terminals and worst section to ground against the 5.0 kV reference, with and without the snubber, and is rendered and inspected. Write paths: scripts/iter/switched_discharge_insertion.py, tests/test_switched_discharge_insertion.py, docs/figures/iter-switched-discharge-insertion, docs/research/iter-switched-discharge-insertion.html, and this section's fragment.

§9 — The switched whole-pulse data the scenario and ripple figures draw

The scenario figure draws each coil's voltage unfiltered, as the whole-pulse switched supply output's extent per time bin, with a peak-to-peak ripple row beneath it (scripts/figures/coil_circuit_playback.py, draw_scenario). It reads the arrays scripts/figures/iter_whole_pulse_ripple.py writes to data/iter/whole_pulse_ripple/, and two gaps keep it from the full figure set. First, the CS arrays predate the CS circulating band. That band was drawn into the source form on 17 October (bridge.CirculatingBridgeGroup, commutation.CS_CIRCULATING_CURRENT_A), but its arrays were written into a worktree and discarded, so the held CS1 ripple row is blank wherever the bridges circulate. Second, the whole-pulse run takes each coil's largest-current SRO case, so PF2 has no switched run of 105069/3, the scenario this plan follows. The PF1 and PF2 edge windows are also coarse (21 samples at a 10 µs step) and predate the integrator fixes.

Rerun the whole-pulse source form for the five CS modules, so that their arrays carry the circulating band, and add a case option so that PF2 runs on 105069/3 beside its own case. Write to the main checkout's data path. Then take one converged switched edge window each for PF1 and PF2 at the steepest commutation edge the ripple figure shows, on the companion or exact integrator, and draw pf2-scenario, pf2-ripple, pf1-edge and pf2-edge through the drawer's draw_scenario and draw_window.

Done when the CS1 ripple row has no blank stretch where its circulating band applies, PF2's scenario and ripple figures draw a switched run of 105069/3, and each PF edge window passes the 1 % step check or is drafted and says so. Every figure is rendered and inspected. Negative control: the CS1 arrays with the circulating band switched off reproduce the held blank stretches.

§10 — PF1's switching-network insertion at initiation, and the insertion rows on the right column

PF1 is one of the three circuits with a switching network: CS1, PF1 and PF6 (778SPD v1.0). The switched builder carries a PF1 row only for the 40 kA design case into 0.210 Ω. It was judged against the 22HLVN fast-discharge column, 2.0 kV, which made its 5.99 kV to ground read as three times over. An insertion is normal operation, so its reference is the nominal column, 12.2 kV for PF1, against which the same peak is 0.49. IDM also sets a limit on the inserted resistor itself: its voltage must stay below 8.5 kV for PF1 (7LDUQJ v1.0 PDF 4). At 105069/3's initiation PF1 carries about 40 kA, and 40 kA through 0.210 Ω is 8.4 kV, close to that limit. No snubber or counterpulse values for the switching network are held, so its front is still run as a ramp over the stated rise-time range (register §5).

Run PF1's switching-network insertion at 105069/3's initiation, as §4 did for CS1: the averaged state at the insertion instant, fronts of 1, 10 and 100 µs, both installed-loss bounds, each at h and h/2, the 1 µs arm also at a tenth of its rise time. Draw pf1-insertion through the drawer's front figure. Restate the PF1, PF6 and CS3L rows of the insertion record against the nominal column, keeping their fast-discharge-column ratios beside it as the record of the earlier reading.

Done when the record gives, for each rise time and bound, PF1's insertion step against the 8.5 kV resistor limit, its peak terminal and worst-section voltage to ground against 12.2 kV, its across-coil peak and its first turn against the 2.5 kV turn-to-turn reference. Each arm passes the 1 % step check or is drafted. The insertion record's PF1, PF6 and CS3L rows read against the nominal column. A peak over a reference is a finding to report, never a defect to fit away. Negative control: with the network bypassed throughout, no insertion step appears.

§11 — CS1's switched ripple window

The ripple figure (draw_ripple) draws a coil's voltage, its current ripple, the current in the neutral grounding resistor against the 0.1 A ground-fault detection threshold, and the voltage spectrum with the 6f to 96f lines and the 2f and 4f imbalance lines marked. PF1 has it, from its held switched window at 303.56 s, and §9 gives PF2 one. CS1 has no switched steady-state window: its held switched rows are the insertion and the fast discharge. The whole-pulse run stores CS1's ripple only as a per-bin extent.

Take one switched window of CS1, 40 ms long, at the steady operating point where the scenario figure's ripple row is largest outside the circulating stretches, on the same plant and grounding as the PF1 window, and draw cs1-ripple.

Done when the window carries coil voltage, coil current and both terminals to ground, its figure is rendered and inspected, and the record states the peak-to-peak current ripple, the peak neutral current against 0.1 A, and the largest line with its order. Negative control: the window's 6f line falls when the bridges circulate, as the circulating band predicts, or the record says it does not.

§12 — The fast-discharge rows at the resistor's scaled inductance and the current at breaker separation

§8's fast-discharge rows rest on two inputs now known better, and on one check that reads the wrong limit.

  • The resistor inductance. The rows use 7LDTQA's magnetostatic table (94.9 → 20.6 µH on CS1). tf-cold-test-validation §13 scaled 48NZDV's measured section through S9BRS4's arrangements: CS and PF units land at 0.73–0.91 of 7LDTQA in the remagnetisation regime, the conservative case for a bipolar coil (IDM register, "FDR transient inductance per unit"). Run the rows at both ends of that range. Take the scaled tables from their owner, scripts/mctb/fdr_inductance.py, in power_convertor.fast_discharge_unit's energy-secant form, and never re-declare them.
  • The interrupted current. The rows open the breaker at the coil's current at the trip. In X7TDMM v2.0's sequence, the breaker-off command comes at about 420 ms and the breaker opens about 22 ms later, about 0.442 s after the trip. Between the two, the converter inverts and is then shunted by the PMS. The counter-pulse is commanded 8 ms after the arc-voltage detector's check-back. So the current the counter-pulse must zero is the coil current at breaker separation. Compute it through the coil circuit and that sequence, and carry G96SWS's timing as a sensitivity. Carry 8 ms of arc at the reported 80 V, a stated assumption from YWDCR5's indexed summary, beside a zero-arc arm.
  • The ordering. A fast discharge is never triggered by a disruption: the trip is t = 0, and any disruption follows it, during the delay, at insertion or in the decay (register row 8025cd1a). No row may place a disruption before its trip.
  • The resistor check. The rows judge the resistor terminals against FDU_RESISTOR_TRANSIENT_V and CS_FDU_RESISTOR_TRANSIENT_V, which give PF2 the generic 7.0 kV. Read the per-group 778SPD maxima from registers/iter_supplies.json instead (discharge_peak_main_breaker_v, discharge_peak_pyrobreaker_v), so PF2 is judged at 7.5 kV and every group carries its own value.

Done when the record states, for CS1U, CS1L and PF2, at both loss bounds, both inductance ends, and with and without the arc:

  • the current at breaker separation;
  • the peak across the current leads, against PA Annex B's 10 kV DC;
  • the peak to ground, beside the 12 kV AC earth-insulation rating as a reference (no approved limit exists);
  • the resistor-terminal peak, against 778SPD's per-group maximum;
  • the first turn, against the 2.5 kV turn-to-turn reference.

It also says whether CS1U's 6.82 kV full-terminal figure moves, and by how much. Each edge window passes the 1 % step check, or is drafted and says so. A crossing is a finding to report against the rating, never a defect to fit away. The fronts figures are redrawn from the new rows through draw_fdu_fronts, both the snubber-fitted figure and its snubber-removed partner, and are rendered and inspected.

Negative controls, each of which must be able to fail:

  • Opening at the trip current instead of at separation moves the peaks by the amount the current difference implies, and the test fails if it does not.
  • With both of §8's inputs restored, 7LDTQA's table and the opening at the trip current, the zero-arc arm reproduces §8's landed values to their pinned tolerance. It does so at each snubber reading and loss bound §8 ran (4 mF and 8 mF, both bounds), because §8's rows carry no arc. Restoring the table alone is logged as a difference against §8's rows, not as a reproduction.

Write paths: scripts/iter/switched_discharge_insertion.py, tests/test_switched_discharge_insertion.py, docs/figures/iter-switched-discharge-insertion, docs/research/iter-switched-discharge-insertion.html, /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/power_convertor/data/iter/switched-discharge-insertion, and the fragment docs/evidence/fragments/coil-circuit-playback-figures/fdu-rows-at-separation.html. Heavy runs go on the fleet allocation, with threads capped at 2.

§ Decisions

Which coil circuits do the figures follow?

PF2 has the winding mode nearest the 600 Hz line and carries VS1; PF1 is a thyristor-only circuit; CS1 carries the switching network and the CS ground limits. One circuit per concern.

One composite figure, or one per concern?

Lead ruling, 19 October 2026, replacing the three-column composite. The scenario figure draws the coil's quantities along the scenario, with the voltage row drawn twice and overlapping: unfiltered in grey, and through a 15 Hz low-pass filter in blue. The ripple, the switching-network insertion and the fast-discharge front each get a separate figure, so each phenomenon is drawn at the window, resolution and references it needs rather than as a narrow column of a composite.

How do the filter cases appear?

The same figure repeated with the filters inserted, the unfiltered response in grey beneath and the filtered one in the highlight colour, styled as the other figures.

Which scenario playback?

The 15 MA H-mode scenario (DINA2024-02), already the base of the held PF switched windows, so every case shares one operating history.

§2 needs no new run and can start now. §3 waits on iter-switched-terminal-transients §6 and §5 on its §11; §4 and §6 follow §2 and, for §6, §3. Figures are reviewed as rendered artefacts in the session, so each node delivers its record, its first render and the render check; layout iteration happens in session afterwards. The lead reviews this plan before anything is dispatched.

One step-convergence owner for the playback record, and one envelope and edge rule

From the design review of 20 October 2026 (findings duplicate_owner-1 and reuse_search-1). It sits with §8, whose rows and front figure are judged by this gate.

  • The record's gate is weaker than the producer's. scripts/iter/switched_discharge_insertion.py's converged compares four pairs: terminal across, terminal high to ground, section across and section to ground. Its convergence_receipt, which the playback record reads, carries only the three to-ground peaks, and the drawer re-declares CONVERGENCE_TOLERANCE = 0.01 beside the owner's CONVERGENCE_TOL. An across-terminal peak can therefore move past 1 % while the figure still draws as converged. The fix: the receipt carries the across pairs, the drawer imports the owner's tolerance and the owner's comparison, and window_receipt reads the same keys. A test checks that a receipt whose across pair moves 2 % is refused.

Carry the TF cold-test commutation uncertainties on the fast-discharge rows

The TF cold-test validation has closed (synthesis, merged at a57aa493; the source rows are in tf-cold-test-commutation). It sends two commutation transfers to this plan's fast-discharge rows, which §8 drew and §12 is rerunning.

  • Timing. The model's current zero is early on every resolved record, by 0.06–0.11 ms, against a measured 0.23–0.49 ms after CPC firing. Carry about 0.1 ms as a timing uncertainty with the model on the fast side. Do not apply it as a correction.
  • Transient peak. On the five September commutations with a measured prefire charge, the model's peak has a median absolute error of 10.5 % with the snubber at the main CCU and 13.3 % with it at the terminal (39.8 kA predicted against 42.8 kA at 30 kA). The data establish neither placement. The six older current shots have no measured prefire charge, so their predictions are conditional, with a sensitivity span of about 6–40 kA.

When §12's rows land, state each FDU row's peak margin against its limit with the larger 13.3 % peak error applied, and the commutation timing as ±0.1 ms with the model on the fast side. Name any row whose margin no longer covers that error. This applies the transfers as uncertainty bands. It changes no row and refits nothing.

The fast-discharge unit's commutation circuit is built in the switched insertion builder from the IDM register's cited values — counterpulse LC, vacuum breaker with its cable, discharge resistor with its stray inductance at both ends of its range, and an RC snubber at both readings — and the CS1 and PF2 fronts are rerun on it, replacing the imposed 10 microsecond ramp. On the lumped coil, which is the model 7JQSNL v1.3 Table 5's peak coil-terminal voltage belongs to, the circuit reproduces U_dr without being fitted to it: CS1 at 49-85 % of 7.6 kV and PF2 at 63-96 % of 4.4 kV, the analytic snubber cap I0 sqrt(L_d/C_s) sitting beside the measured peak, and the discharge resistor inside S9BRS4's 10 kV at every one of the eight rows (worst 43.1 %; the plant's twelve arms run 6.6 to 59.3 %). The declared negative control is the snubber's removal, logged with its size at 5.61 x on CS1 and 65.1 x on PF2, and the second declared arm — the first-turn pin — is run with its mutation alone and fails it. On the plant the same edge rings the sectioned winding far past 22HLVN v1.0's fast-discharge column and 14 x the lumped reading of the same across-terminal quantity; that is reported as a model over-response with its cause, and the to-ground check stays on the lumped model the IDM value belongs to. Against the across reference the unit is inside U_dr on both coils; its peak coil-terminal voltage to ground on PF2 is not. §8: the plant FDU row over-responds because the builder opens the vacuum breaker at the analytic counterpulse instant t_z = 99.3630 µs, where the modelled branch still carries 9385.3 A — its own current zero is 127.2126 µs, 27.85 µs later. That current commutates into the feeder line (0.378 nF, 87.27 ohm surge impedance) and the winding capacitances instead of into the 4 mF snubber as on the lumped coil, giving 90323.6 V across against the lumped 6432.2 V (14.04x) and 58203.6 V to ground. Opening the breaker at its own current zero gives 6646.7 V across and 3329.6 V to ground, within 3.3% of the lumped 6432.2 V, and the two models then agree to 0.1%; the sections' part in it is disproved, not confirmed — removing the winding ground or cross capacitances makes the peak worse (290015.8 V, 140716.5 V). The fix is a builder change to open on the branch current rather than the analytic instant, reported and not applied because scripts/iter/switched_discharge_insertion.py is outside this node's write scope and owned by a concurrent node.

Correction to c-s8-breaker-zero: the MCTB breaker current zero is 0.27–0.49 ms after counterpulse firing, measured, 0.15–0.17 ms after the analytic instant. The 1.96 ms quoted there was the controller's computed time and is withdrawn. The conclusion, that the breaker opens at its own zero after the analytic instant, stands. evidence

Second correction to the MCTB comparison, after c-s8-mctb-correction. The 0.15–0.17 ms lag of the measured breaker zero behind the analytic instant was mostly the measurement operator: a 21-sample mean and an onset threshold, about 0.14 ms. Read with the same operator, the model that opens the breaker at its own current zero lies within about 0.03 ms of the measured zero at TF17 30 kA (tf-cold-test-validation). This supports opening at the branch's own zero and gives no physical lag to add. The register row "MCTB TF cold-test FDU" carries the values (866685d9).
